top.title: Willie Fritz on expanded College Football Playoff and Cougars' chances this year | UH football notes
top.description: Houston Cougars fans celebrate after wide receiver Amare Thomas' 8-yard touchdown catch during an NCAA college football game in Houston, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) University of Houston coach Willie Fritz said Monday that he supports the expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams, saying the new format will give more programs access to the postseason. The CFP will double in size beginning in 2027, part of a five-year deal between ESPN and the CFP announced Monday, while also eliminating Power Four conference championship games. "I think it gives more people access," Fritz said at his weekly press conference to preview Friday's game at Colorado. "I think people are thirsty for college football and quality games, and that will certainly give you more." BOHLS: Expansion to 24 teams is wrong, greedy and bad for sport The 24-team field will include 19 at-large bids, the Power Four champions as determined by each league, plus the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The Big 12 announced Monday that this year's conference championship game, Dec. 4 in Arlington, will be its last. Beginning next year, the regular-season champion will receive the Big 12's automatic bid. In a 24-team field, UH - which was No. 17 in the first CFP rankings - would be in good position to receive an at-large bid and be in position to host a first-round game on campus. REACTION: What coaches are saying The Cougars are still in the hunt for this season's 12-team field, needing to win their final three games and have Texas Tech lose once. In that scenario, UH would win most of the tiebreakers involving multiple two-loss teams and advance to the Big 12 championship game. The Cougars' current CFP ranking is the highest in program history. "You want to be relevant," Fritz said. "We certainly want Houston to be out there front and center as much as possible. So that's great. But you've got to finish the year, and you've got to keep playing well. Being ranked right now doesn't mean a whole lot. You want to be ranked as high as we can at the end of the season. That means we've accomplished some things." A positive return Linebacker Jaden Yates had a team-high nine tackles Saturday after missing a month with a lower-body injury. Yates suffered the injury in Week 5 against UCF and missed the next three games before returning after the open week. "I thought he did a good job," Fritz said. "He doesn't seem to have any side effects from the injury. There are a lot of things that he does for us back there." Yates has the green dot on the back of his helmet, which signifies he is equipped with a coach-to-player radio communication system. Part of Yates' responsibility is to relay instructions from defensive coordinator Austin Armstrong to the rest of the unit and help with alignment. When he was out, that responsibility fell to Sione Fotu and Carmycah Glass. "I think (Yates) knocked a lot of the rust off and will play even better this week," Fritz said.

top.title: Why I believe Carson Benge should have won NL Rookie of the Year
top.description: The Major League Baseball season's characterization as a "marathon" is more appropriate than any other professional sport. There are plenty of ebbs and flows over the course of the 162-game season. Performances can't be defined by a single month or stretch of time. The extensive nature of the campaign is what made the National League race for Rookie of the Year one of the most contentious contests in the MLB Award season. Over the course of six months, five candidates rose to the top in the Reds' Sal Stewart, Mets' Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt and Rockies' TJ Rumfield. In the end, it was Stewart who was named the NL Rookie of the Year honor as the Baseball Writers Association of American announced the award on Monday night. Stewart took home the honor on the strength of his 32 home runs and 112 RBI, which led all NL rookies, along with 87 runs, a .787 OPS, 25 doubles and 15 stolen bases. Stewart earned 20 of the 30 possible first-place votes. The Mets' Benge ended up as the runner-up with seven first-place votes, three second-place votes and 12 third-place designations. One of those votes for Benge to receive the top honor was mine. When the BBWAA assigned its award designations to the writers in early August, the Rookie of the Year race appeared to be a two-horse race between Stewart and Wetherholt. But over the the final two months of the season, Benge's kick provided further intrigue. That's why the season is a marathon. And by the completion of the 2026 season, I believe Benge had done enough in all facets of the game to warrant the top slot in the Rookie of the Year vote. Stewart's explosive bat made him a top contender. The Reds first baseman had the second-most RBI and eighth-most home runs in the National League while he slashed .263/.330/.457. Wetherholt proved he had one of the best gloves in all of baseball, boasting a +25 outs above average that trailed only Cubs MVP frontrunner Pete Crow-Armstrong for the best mark in baseball. While batting atop the Cardinals' lineup, the second baseman led all rookies with 89 runs, while adding 17 home runs, 51 RBI and 14 stolen bases but posting an unassuming .242/.339/.365 slash line in 139 games. Benge provided the best of both worlds in terms of offense and defense despite a slow start through the opening two months, which hurt his case in the early going. The Mets right-fielder led all rookies with 168 hits — matching the Tigers' Kevin McGonigle in the American League — and was second among NL rookies in batting average (.282) and home runs (20) and third in RBI (65) and stolen bases (22). Benge is the only NL rookie to finish in the top three in each of those key offensive categories. Most of that production came after Benge opened with a .189 batting average and .525 OPS through the month of April. He slashed .299/.363/.457 over the final five months. top.title: Vikings-Bills live discussion: A chaotic matchup between a pair of overrated teams
top.description: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-1 Buffalo Bills take on the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings. These are two of the best teams in the NFL record-wise, but they are from the most complete teams. The Vikings’ offense has been asleep at the wheel all season. Justin Jefferson is on pace for a career worst year. He won’t have Kyler Murray throwing him the ball tonight, but that might be a blessing in disguise, as Murray tends to be erratic and miss open receivers downfield. What Minnesota lacks offensively, they more than make up for it on the defensive side of the ball. They are comfortably the best stop unit in the league, thanks in large part to their ability to prevent success against the pass. Brian Flores blitzes over 3/4 of the time, and invites chaotic play. If there’s a quarterback who thrives in chaos, it’s Josh Allen. Allen makes play after play, usually off-script. He’s down left tackle Dion Dawkins, which might invite Allen to run more. I can see Allen and James Cook having big days on the ground, and Khalil Shakir pitching in on key third downs. The Bills are lousy defensively. They’ve allowed 33, 31, 29, 34, and 30 points this season. So, if there was a get-right spot for Carson Wentz, Jefferson, and the Vikings, it’s the Bills’ defense that gave up 30 points to the Raiders team we just watched. My gut says the NFC’s strength tops the AFC’s in this game, and the Vikings eke out a win. But going against Allen is asking for it. Deep down, I think these are two overrated teams that’ll be exposed come playoff time.

top.title: Sal Stewart named NL Rookie of the Year
top.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MAY 27: Sal Stewart #27 of the Cincinnati Reds in action against the New York Mets at Citi Field on May 27, 2026 in New York City. The Mets defeated the Reds 4-2. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Reds first baseman Sal Stewart has been named NL Rookie of the Year, taking home 20 of 30 first place votes en route to a comfortable win. Stewart takes home the award on the back of a .263/.330/.457 season (112 wRC+) with 32 HR and 112 RBI, with 15 steals tacked on to boot. Carson Benge finished second, while Nolan McLean finished 4th. Benge was named a finalist for the award alongside JJ Wetherholdt and Stewart last week. Thomas Henderson profiled each of those finalists earlier today , concluding that Stewart was the likeliest to win on the back of his 30 homer season. Indeed, Stewart has already been named Sporting News Rookie of the Year , a version of award voted on by players rather than writers. Earlier today ahead of the official announcement, betting odds (per Kalshi) had Stewart as a shoe-in for the official version of the award. While it’s easy to understand why Stewart has supporters (Dingerz, baby), his analytical case is quite poor. Wetherholdt and Benge were both far superior players by all WAR metrics, and even other rookies like TJ Rumfield and Joe Mack were more valuable overall contributors. A.J. Ewing, who tallied only 492 AB to Stewarts’s 700, was nearly as valuable in his own right. At least three rookies on the mound – Logan Henderson, Andrew Alvarez, and Nolan McLean – were also more valuable players. In prior years, this would’ve been a mild annoyance to debate in chat threads or on Twitter, but with the implementation of the Prospect Promotion Incentive (PPI) system there are actual stakes here. For the Mets, this is a frustrating and somewhat damaging outcome. Despite having two of the three best rookies in Benge and McLean, the org will not receive anything in the way of draft pick awards, a boon that would’ve greatly helped their eternally challenged draft pool.

top.title: Michael Carrick on the brink at Manchester United amid club review
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester United manager Michael Carrick applauds the fans after the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and Aston Villa at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Michael Carrick on the brink at Manchester United amid club review») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Michael Carrick's days as Manchester United head coach appear to be numbered as the club reviews his position and considers alternatives. The Red Devils will spend the international break in the relegation zone after failing to add to August's solitary Premier League win against Ipswich in Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. United languish in 18th spot and are reviewing Carrick's position as the club take stock during the international break, the Press Association understands. Reports suggest the club intend to replace the former midfielder following talks on Monday, although Old Trafford sources insisted no decision had been made that evening. United director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada seriously considered sacking Carrick a fortnight ago after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth compounded a calamitous 4-1 Champions League loss at Como. The club eventually decided to give the head coach and his players the opportunity to turn the situation around before the international break. Carrick's side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday's 3-2 comeback win against Roma and Sunday's 4-4 draw with Villa. United have been considering whether that run merits him staying on and would have to push a manager who headed into the international break having stressed he would not walk away. Asked if the November pause comes at a good time for the group, the under-fire United boss said: "Yeah, it's been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you're looking at the events. "But I'm pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there. "Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so. "But as a normal international week is, you know, we'll have some training. We'll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we'll train, and we'll get ready for the next game." The final international break of the year would seem a logical time if United wanted to make a change, given there is no free midweek until mid-December after returning with a trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22. Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann are contenders to replace Carrick if the club decide a change in the Old Trafford hotseat is necessary. Mauricio Pochettino, the former Tottenham, Paris St Germain and Chelsea manager, has often been linked with the role and bookmakers have slashed odds on him coming in. top.title: Army-Navy game moves up a week to accommodate expanded CFP
top.description: Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images One second-order effect of the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams is the annual Army-Navy game, which has traditionally been held on the second weekend of December, following conference championship weekend. With ESPN and the CFP officially announcing the expansion to 24 teams on Monday, the Army-Navy game also officially got its new date. Next year’s Army-Navy game will be played on Saturday, Dec. 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, one week earlier than the originally scheduled date of Dec. 11. The game, which is broadcast annually by CBS, will now be played the week following rivalry week, which is the last official week of the regular season. Army-Navy will now occupy the Saturday that used to be reserved for a full slate of conference championship games. The Army-Navy Game announced today that the 2027 Army-Navy Game presented by USAA, the 128th playing of America’s Game, will be played Saturday, Dec. 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. The date change from Dec. 11 was necessitated by the CFP moving to 24 teams and starting on Dec. 9. → https://t.co/lCIx6Pbqmp #ArmyNavy — Army-Navy Game (@ArmyNavyGame) November 9, 2026 Where to put the Army-Navy game in an expanded CFP format was often a footnote in discussions about potential expansion until President Trump signed an executive order earlier this year mandating that the annual matchup between the two service academies have its own standalone time slot, free of any other FBS games. Moving the game to the first weekend of December should allow for that, as conference championship games will no longer occupy those television windows. “We are thankful to the city of Philadelphia and Lincoln Financial Field for their efforts to manage the date change of the 2027 Army-Navy Game to ensure the Game is played in its exclusive time slot on CBS,” Tom Theodorakis, director of athletics and chief executive officer of Army West Point Athletic Association, said in an announcement . “As we look ahead to future games, we are excited about the opportunity to build on our strong foundation and secure new commitments that demonstrate a shared passion to grow the game and drive economic impact in host cities.” “We appreciate the flexibility of the people of Philadelphia to accommodate this date change, and we applaud the collaboration between the city of Philadelphia, Lincoln Financial Field and the academies,” Michael Kelly, Director of Athletics of the Naval Academy and President of the Naval Academy Athletic Association, said in Monday’s release. “We are also extremely grateful to the CFP leadership for their collaboration. Finding a way to preserve the exclusive broadcast window for America’s Game while ensuring our program has a rightful path to compete in the College Football Playoff is a tremendous outcome for our student-athletes and fans across the country.” The post Army-Navy game moves up a week to accommodate expanded CFP appeared first

top.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
top.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. top.title: Bill Belichick’s ex-girlfriend Jordon Hudson sues Mass. couple over viral Ring camera video
top.description: Former NFL head coach Bill Belichick and girlfriend Jordon Hudson, pose on the red carpet at the NFL Honors award show ahead of the Super Bowl 59 football game, Thursday, Feb. 6, 2025, in New Orleans. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson) Brynn Anderson The former girlfriend of Bill Belichick is suing a Winthrop couple, alleging they violated her privacy by sharing the now-viral Ring camera video of Belichick and disclosing private information about their relationship. Hudson is suing Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan, the owners of the property she booked through Airbnb in June 2023. The 20-page complaint, filed on Nov. 6 in Suffolk Superior Court, states that Hudson and Belichick were keeping their relationship private at the time of the video leak. According to the complaint, a Ring camera outside of the home captured the video of Belichick walking around shirtless. In a text thread, Hudson wrote that McDevitt sent her the video during their stay, but assured her that it would be deleted. The complaint states the video later appeared on social media in November 2023 and was picked up by news outlets. Additional text threads included in the document from McDevitt show her initially denying leaking it. McDevitt wrote, “I absolutely did not leak this video to twitter or anyone.” However, the lawsuit states that McDevitt later wrote in another text that she and Nolan shared the videos with others, writing, “We had sent it to a few people initially wondering is this him [Mr. Belichick], isn’t it him.” The complaint alleged that sharing the video led to the leak and contributed to the public learning of Hudson’s relationship with Belichick. Hudson also alleged that the hosts disclosed additional information about their stay on a podcast. The complaint also alleged the couple looked through a window during their stay. Hudson stated she later reported the hosts to Airbnb. Airbnb determined its privacy policy was violated and removed the property from its platform. Documents also alleged that McDevitt messaged Hudson, “You’re not even famous now! You are infamous. Good for you!” Hudson is seeking unspecified damages as well as a court order preventing the defendants from disclosing additional private information about her. This is a developing story. In Dipoto’s first season, the Mariners trended towards conservative hires or retaining coaches who had already been in the organization. Dipoto brought over several people he’d worked with during his time with the Angels – Mike Micucci, Ethan Katz, and Zac Livingston – and retained most other staff members rather than cleaning house organizationally from top to bottom. But by 2016, Dipoto and then-Director of Player Development Andy McKay were ready to take some bigger swings. One of the biggest was hiring a 32-year-old Mitch Canham to manage their A-ball affiliate, the Clinton LumberKings. At the time, Canham was well-known to Northwest baseball fans as a standout star at Lake Stevens high school and then Oregon State, but an unknown quantity in the broader coaching world, lacking any official managerial experience before being handed the reins at a full-season affiliate. Canham’s hiring was part of an organizational philosophy shift that emphasized quality of leadership over depth of experience – as McKay put it, “ better people make better baseball players ”, which starts with them being led by the best people available. nigeria.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages. The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia. According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future. The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services. It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development. Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers. “Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need. “That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth. “We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said. Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program. The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities. It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026. The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026. The transition to a permanent programme is expected to provide rural employers with a more reliable supply of skilled foreign workers while supporting the long-term economic development of participating communities. nigeria.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors. Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors. According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state. He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.” Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters. He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration. Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions. He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates. The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration. “That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said. Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector. nigeria.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028, suspect faces death penalty
nigeria.description: The trial of the man accused of murdering US conservative firebrand Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, the judge said Monday. “Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028,” judge Tony Graf told the Utah district court, noting that 105 days have been reserved for the trial. Tyler Robinson, 23, faces a potential death penalty for allegedly killing Kirk with a gunshot to the neck on a university campus in the western US state of Utah on September 10, 2025. The killing of Kirk at age 31 at an event planned by his right-wing youth organization, Turning Point, sent shockwaves through the US political world. Kirk had become a popular leader in a Christian Nationalist movement that preaches traditional values while voicing intolerance for diversity and LGBTQ communities. Turning Point was key to mobilizing youth support for Donald Trump’s re-election as president in 2024. The group is now led by his wife, Erika Kirk. The prosecution had sought a trial as early as January 2028, while Robinson’s lawyers had wanted until the end of 2029 to prepare their defense. Last month, Trump criticized the judge and said the case “should be tried within a month, not three years.” Kirk’s assassination last year triggered a 33-hour manhunt culminating in Robinson surrendering to authorities. He has pled not guilty. The prosecution has presented text messages in which Robinson confessed to planning the murder to his roommate, a transgender person with whom they allege Robinson was in a relationship. The defense has focused on alleged weaknesses in the DNA and ballistic evidence. nigeria.title: Manchester United are becoming a club of survival rather than ambition
nigeria.description: The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen. There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation. Those expectations seem increasingly distant. On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience. But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant. Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory. That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse. United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches . They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League. The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success. Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend. Survival has become the immediate ambition. And that is a remarkable development for a club whose history was built on refusing to accept anything less than excellence. nigeria.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
nigeria.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days. According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), participating communities will approve designated employers to recruit skilled foreign nationals for available positions. To qualify for permanent residence under the programme, applicants must obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community and secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within that community. They must also have at least one year, equivalent to 1,560 hours, of related work experience within the previous three years. Other requirements include demonstrating language proficiency through an approved test, possessing a Canadian educational credential or its foreign equivalent, and providing proof of sufficient funds to support themselves and their families. Valid job offer: Secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within the participating community. Work experience: Have at least one year (1,560 hours) of related work experience within the past three years. Language proficiency: Demonstrate English or French language ability by taking an approved language test. Educational qualification: Possess a Canadian educational credential or a foreign equivalent. Proof of funds: Provide evidence of having sufficient money to support themselves and their families after arriving in Canada. The programme is designed to help participating rural communities attract skilled foreign nationals while providing immigrants with an opportunity to obtain permanent residence and establish themselves in Canada. That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager. The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Elliptic’s wider update now puts roughly 3,000 BTC — about $225 million — in new bitcoin addresses converted from other stolen assets, while about 11.8 million NEAR, or $43.7 million, from the theft has still not moved. “Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype,” Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson wrote. “North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them.” How the homemade token trick works The technique is a four-step hop. The North Korea launderers create a token with a public launch tool, open a liquidity pool pairing it with a real asset such as NEAR or a stablecoin, buy the new token with stolen funds from one set of wallets, then sell it back into the same pool from a second set of wallets that collect the real asset. At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. To a casual observer, the collecting wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit. Each of the six NEAR tokens cost about 25 NEAR, or around $90, to create. Five of the six token creators were funded by a wallet that had just sold an earlier token, between two and 13 minutes before the next launch, so the tokens form a chain. A slowing tactic, not a disappearing act The meme coins do not hide the funds. Every step is public on-chain. What they buy is time. entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. sports.description: Houston Cougars fans celebrate after wide receiver Amare Thomas' 8-yard touchdown catch during an NCAA college football game in Houston, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) University of Houston coach Willie Fritz said Monday that he supports the expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams, saying the new format will give more programs access to the postseason. The CFP will double in size beginning in 2027, part of a five-year deal between ESPN and the CFP announced Monday, while also eliminating Power Four conference championship games. "I think it gives more people access," Fritz said at his weekly press conference to preview Friday's game at Colorado. "I think people are thirsty for college football and quality games, and that will certainly give you more." BOHLS: Expansion to 24 teams is wrong, greedy and bad for sport The 24-team field will include 19 at-large bids, the Power Four champions as determined by each league, plus the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The Big 12 announced Monday that this year's conference championship game, Dec. 4 in Arlington, will be its last. Beginning next year, the regular-season champion will receive the Big 12's automatic bid. In a 24-team field, UH - which was No. 17 in the first CFP rankings - would be in good position to receive an at-large bid and be in position to host a first-round game on campus. REACTION: What coaches are saying The Cougars are still in the hunt for this season's 12-team field, needing to win their final three games and have Texas Tech lose once. In that scenario, UH would win most of the tiebreakers involving multiple two-loss teams and advance to the Big 12 championship game. The Cougars' current CFP ranking is the highest in program history. "You want to be relevant," Fritz said. "We certainly want Houston to be out there front and center as much as possible. So that's great. But you've got to finish the year, and you've got to keep playing well. Being ranked right now doesn't mean a whole lot. You want to be ranked as high as we can at the end of the season. That means we've accomplished some things." A positive return Linebacker Jaden Yates had a team-high nine tackles Saturday after missing a month with a lower-body injury. Yates suffered the injury in Week 5 against UCF and missed the next three games before returning after the open week. "I thought he did a good job," Fritz said. "He doesn't seem to have any side effects from the injury. There are a lot of things that he does for us back there." Yates has the green dot on the back of his helmet, which signifies he is equipped with a coach-to-player radio communication system. Part of Yates' responsibility is to relay instructions from defensive coordinator Austin Armstrong to the rest of the unit and help with alignment. When he was out, that responsibility fell to Sione Fotu and Carmycah Glass. "I think (Yates) knocked a lot of the rust off and will play even better this week," Fritz said.

sports.title: Why I believe Carson Benge should have won NL Rookie of the Year
sports.description: The Major League Baseball season's characterization as a "marathon" is more appropriate than any other professional sport. There are plenty of ebbs and flows over the course of the 162-game season. Performances can't be defined by a single month or stretch of time. The extensive nature of the campaign is what made the National League race for Rookie of the Year one of the most contentious contests in the MLB Award season. sports.title: Vikings-Bills live discussion: A chaotic matchup between a pair of overrated teams
sports.description: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-1 Buffalo Bills take on the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings. These are two of the best teams in the NFL record-wise, but they are from the most complete teams. The Vikings’ offense has been asleep at the wheel all season. Justin Jefferson is on pace for a career worst year. He won’t have Kyler Murray throwing him the ball tonight, but that might be a blessing in disguise, as Murray tends to be erratic and miss open receivers downfield. What Minnesota lacks offensively, they more than make up for it on the defensive side of the ball. They are comfortably the best stop unit in the league, thanks in large part to their ability to prevent success against the pass. Brian Flores blitzes over 3/4 of the time, and invites chaotic play. If there’s a quarterback who thrives in chaos, it’s Josh Allen. Allen makes play after play, usually off-script. He’s down left tackle Dion Dawkins, which might invite Allen to run more. I can see Allen and James Cook having big days on the ground, and Khalil Shakir pitching in on key third downs. The Bills are lousy defensively. They’ve allowed 33, 31, 29, 34, and 30 points this season. So, if there was a get-right spot for Carson Wentz, Jefferson, and the Vikings, it’s the Bills’ defense that gave up 30 points to the Raiders team we just watched. My gut says the NFC’s strength tops the AFC’s in this game, and the Vikings eke out a win. But going against Allen is asking for it. Deep down, I think these are two overrated teams that’ll be exposed come playoff time.

Benge was named a finalist for the award alongside JJ Wetherholdt and Stewart last week. Thomas Henderson profiled each of those finalists earlier today , concluding that Stewart was the likeliest to win on the back of his 30 homer season. While it’s easy to understand why Stewart has supporters (Dingerz, baby), his analytical case is quite poor. The Red Devils will spend the international break in the relegation zone after failing to add to August's solitary Premier League win against Ipswich in Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. United languish in 18th spot and are reviewing Carrick's position as the club take stock during the international break, the Press Association understands. sports.title: Army-Navy game moves up a week to accommodate expanded CFP
sports.description: Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images One second-order effect of the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams is the annual Army-Navy game, which has traditionally been held on the second weekend of December, following conference championship weekend. With ESPN and the CFP officially announcing the expansion to 24 teams on Monday, the Army-Navy game also officially got its new date. Next year’s Army-Navy game will be played on Saturday, Dec. 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, one week earlier than the originally scheduled date of Dec. 11. The game, which is broadcast annually by CBS, will now be played the week following rivalry week, which is the last official week of the regular season. Army-Navy will now occupy the Saturday that used to be reserved for a full slate of conference championship games. The Army-Navy Game announced today that the 2027 Army-Navy Game presented by USAA, the 128th playing of America’s Game, will be played Saturday, Dec. 4 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. The date change from Dec. 11 was necessitated by the CFP moving to 24 teams and starting on Dec. 9. → https://t.co/lCIx6Pbqmp #ArmyNavy — Army-Navy Game (@ArmyNavyGame) November 9, 2026 Where to put the Army-Navy game in an expanded CFP format was often a footnote in discussions about potential expansion until President Trump signed an executive order earlier this year mandating that the annual matchup between the two service academies have its own standalone time slot, free of any other FBS games. Moving the game to the first weekend of December should allow for that, as conference championship games will no longer occupy those television windows. “We are thankful to the city of Philadelphia and Lincoln Financial Field for their efforts to manage the date change of the 2027 Army-Navy Game to ensure the Game is played in its exclusive time slot on CBS,” Tom Theodorakis, director of athletics and chief executive officer of Army West Point Athletic Association, said in an announcement . “As we look ahead to future games, we are excited about the opportunity to build on our strong foundation and secure new commitments that demonstrate a shared passion to grow the game and drive economic impact in host cities.” “We appreciate the flexibility of the people of Philadelphia to accommodate this date change, and we applaud the collaboration between the city of Philadelphia, Lincoln Financial Field and the academies,” Michael Kelly, Director of Athletics of the Naval Academy and President of the Naval Academy Athletic Association, said in Monday’s release. “We are also extremely grateful to the CFP leadership for their collaboration. Hudson is suing Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan, the owners of the property she booked through Airbnb in June 2023. The 20-page complaint, filed on Nov. 6 in Suffolk Superior Court, states that Hudson and Belichick were keeping their relationship private at the time of the video leak. According to the complaint, a Ring camera outside of the home captured the video of Belichick walking around shirtless. In a text thread, Hudson wrote that McDevitt sent her the video during their stay, but assured her that it would be deleted. The complaint states the video later appeared on social media in November 2023 and was picked up by news outlets. Additional text threads included in the document from McDevitt show her initially denying leaking it. McDevitt wrote, “I absolutely did not leak this video to twitter or anyone.” However, the lawsuit states that McDevitt later wrote in another text that she and Nolan shared the videos with others, writing, “We had sent it to a few people initially wondering is this him [Mr. Belichick], isn’t it him.” The complaint alleged that sharing the video led to the leak and contributed to the public learning of Hudson’s relationship with Belichick. Hudson also alleged that the hosts disclosed additional information about their stay on a podcast. The complaint also alleged the couple looked through a window during their stay. Hudson stated she later reported the hosts to Airbnb. Airbnb determined its privacy policy was violated and removed the property from its platform. Documents also alleged that McDevitt messaged Hudson, “You’re not even famous now! You are infamous. Dipoto brought over several people he’d worked with during his time with the Angels – Mike Micucci, Ethan Katz, and Zac Livingston – and retained most other staff members rather than cleaning house organizationally from top to bottom. But by 2016, Dipoto and then-Director of Player Development Andy McKay were ready to take some bigger swings. One of the biggest was hiring a 32-year-old Mitch Canham to manage their A-ball affiliate, the Clinton LumberKings. At the time, Canham was well-known to Northwest baseball fans as a standout star at Lake Stevens high school and then Oregon State, but an unknown quantity in the broader coaching world, lacking any official managerial experience before being handed the reins at a full-season affiliate. Canham’s hiring was part of an organizational philosophy shift that emphasized quality of leadership over depth of experience – as McKay put it, “ better people make better baseball players ”, which starts with them being led by the best people available. Joining Canham in Clinton was pitching coach Pete Woodworth, who had more official coaching experience but was just 28 years old at the time. Those hires sparked an influx of young coaching talent, often from non-traditional coaching backgrounds, into the Mariners organization. The next few years would see the hiring of at the time relatively unknown names, many of whom who have since moved on from Seattle to build impressive coaching resumes elsewhere: Tony Arnerich, Carson Vitale, Hugh Quattlebaum, Max Weiner, Jarret DeHart, Rob Marcello, Sean McGrath, just to name a handful. Those coaches oversaw the transition of the Mariners farm system from one of the worst in baseball to a consistent solid performer, and the pitching coaches especially helped the Mariners earn a well-deserved reputation as one of the sport’s best in developing pitchers. But the Mariners paid the price – or rather, didn’t – for that innovation, losing many of their young coaches to better opportunities (and/or better salaries) elsewhere. Two that stung the most were the losses of Canham and Weiner, both of whom moved on to high-profile (and high-paid) jobs at the college level. Qubole is a cloud data processing platform that uses cross-account IAM roles to manage compute and access storage in customers' AWS environments without requiring customers to provide long-lived AWS access keys. The supply-chain attack abused this third-party, cross-account trust relationship. Google’s cloud-security shop Wiz declined to tell us how many organizations were affected, but called it a “broad, opportunistic supply chain campaign” that hit “multiple” customer environments. “Because many organizations left trust policies active even after deprecating the platform, the attacker was able to successfully assume integration roles, enumerate cloud resources, harvest secrets, and siphon data,” the researchers told The Register in an emailed response to questions. Neither AWS nor Qubole responded to The Register 's inquiries. Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders after AI data security company Sentra flagged suspicious activity, traced the malicious activity back to October 14, when credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account were used to call the sts:AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for customer-managed integration roles. The calls originated from Qubole AWS account 805246085872 , and used IAM user ID AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS , Wiz analysts Zack Morrow, Sean Johnstone, and Benjamin Read said in a Monday blog about the supply chain attack. “Across the affected environments, Wiz CIRT has not observed this IAM user in any activity other than that associated with this threat actor,” the trio wrote. This activity continued on October 15, and on October 18, the digital intruders began using a second IAM user from the same account. Once inside customers’ environments, the crooks began probing a ton of AWS services and stealing credentials, keys, and other secrets stored across Lambda, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store. science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. science.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. The luminous blue variable and supernova impostor AT 2016blu is in the middle of the small square. X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said. science.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
science.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them." Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event . Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd. The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group. But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them. "The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved." "We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night . We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base.
